title: Pistachio and Raspberry Tart
changes_from_base: A baked pistachio paste filling studded with raspberries, replacing the crème pâtissière and fresh fruit.
summary: A crisp lemon pastry case filled with a rich baked pistachio paste and scattered with raspberries.
equipment: 23 cm fluted tart tin, 2.5 cm deep

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, in 2 cm pieces

ingredients.note: you may not need it all

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: blitz the flour, sugar, salt, zest and butter for about 15 seconds, to fine crumbs. With the motor running add the lemon juice, then the water a spoonful at a time, stopping once the dough forms. Wrap and chill 30 min.

steps.title: Line the tin
steps.text: roll to a 33 cm round about 2 mm thick, ease it into the tin and press it into the corners. Trim 5 mm above the rim and chill 30 min.

steps.title: Blind bake
steps.text: heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Line with paper and beans and bake 25 min, until golden at the edge, then remove the paper and beans and bake 8 min more. Turn the oven down to 175 °C (155 °C fan).

steps.title: Paste
steps.text: roast the pistachios on a tray for 8 min, until hot but not coloured. Set 100 g aside on the board. Process the rest while still hot for 6-8 min, scraping down often, until a thick, smooth paste forms. Pulse in the melted butter, zest, lemon juice, flavourings and salt. Chop the reserved nuts roughly. The nuts must be hot to turn into a smooth paste.

steps.title: Batter
steps.text: whisk the eggs on high for 3-4 min, to soft peaks. On medium, add the sugar slowly, then on low mix in the flour, pistachio paste and chopped nuts.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: spread the filling in the case, scatter the raspberries over and bake about 35 min, until golden at the edges and set in the middle. Cool on the rack before slicing. A few raspberries will sink, which is fine.

tips: A powerful food processor makes the paste much easier.
Use raw, unsalted pistachios, not roasted salted ones.
Shop-bought pure pistachio paste (220 g) can replace the homemade paste.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day, or in the fridge for up to 3 days.
